original_question: Let X be an Enriques surface and let Ku(X, L) be the Kuznetsov component in a semiorthogonal decomposition Db(X) = <Ku(X, L), L>. Do the Fourier-Mukai existence questions from Questions 1.7 and 1.8 have a positive answer when D_i is taken to be a Kuznetsov component Ku(X_i, L_i) of an Enriques surface?
target_in_paper: Question 3.9(iii), namely the Enriques-surface specialization of the general Fourier-Mukai questions from Section 2: whether Question 2.7 or Question 2.8 has a positive answer when the admissible subcategories are Kuznetsov components Ku(X_i, L_i) of Enriques surfaces. This is the exact open problem later linked to removing the Fourier-Mukai hypothesis in Theorem 4.5.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant geometric setting (Enriques surfaces), the relevant admissible subcategories (their Kuznetsov components Ku(X, L)), and the fact that the paper asks a Fourier-Mukai existence/type question for these components. It also correctly senses the connection with the Fourier-Mukai assumption appearing in the Enriques categorical Torelli theorem.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation in the paper is not a free-standing restatement of Questions 2.7 and 2.8, but Question 3.9(iii), which explicitly specializes those general questions to the Enriques Kuznetsov component.
The paper works over an algebraically closed field K throughout, and in the Enriques section assumes char(K) ≠ 2.
The problem concerns two admissible subcategories Ku(X_1, L_1) and Ku(X_2, L_2), so the quantification over two Enriques surfaces and two choices of exceptional collections should be made explicit.
Ku(X, L) depends on the chosen exceptional collection L, not only on the surface X; the paper stresses this dependence.

Your decomposition D^b(X) = <Ku(X, L), L> is only the simplified generic/no-(-2)-curves picture from Example 3.8. In the general Enriques setup of Proposition 3.7 and Section 4.2, the orthogonal part is organized into blocks, so the question should refer to the Kuznetsov component arising from the semiorthogonal decompositions considered there.

The paper distinguishes the stronger and weaker Fourier-Mukai questions: Question 2.7 asks whether every exact fully faithful functor is of Fourier-Mukai type, whereas Question 2.8 asks only whether an exact equivalence can be replaced by some Fourier-Mukai equivalence.
To be self-contained, the meaning of 'of Fourier-Mukai type' should be stated: after composing with the admissible embeddings into D^b(X_i), the functor is induced by a kernel in D^b(X_1 × X_2).

If you want the question to reflect the paper's motivation, it should mention that a positive answer would remove the explicit Fourier-Mukai-type assumption from the Enriques categorical Torelli theorem in Theorem 4.5, as stated in Remark 4.6(ii).
refined_question: Let K be an algebraically closed field with char(K) ≠ 2. For i = 1, 2, let X_i be Enriques surfaces over K, and let Ku(X_i, L_i) be the Kuznetsov component arising from a semiorthogonal decomposition of D^b(X_i) of the type considered in Proposition 3.7 and Section 4.2, so that Ku(X_i, L_i) depends on the chosen exceptional collection L_i. Does the Enriques-surface specialization of the Fourier-Mukai problem have a positive answer: namely, is every exact fully faithful functor F: Ku(X_1, L_1) → Ku(X_2, L_2) of Fourier-Mukai type (in the sense of Definition 2.6, i.e. induced, after composing with the admissible embeddings, by a kernel on X_1 × X_2), or at least, whenever F is an exact equivalence, does there exist some Fourier-Mukai equivalence Ku(X_1, L_1) ≅ Ku(X_2, L_2)?
justification: This is the paper-faithful sharpening of your draft because the authors themselves isolate exactly this Enriques-specific specialization as Question 3.9(iii), after introducing the general Fourier-Mukai questions in Questions 2.7 and 2.8 and the notion of Fourier-Mukai type in Definition 2.6. The surrounding Enriques context, including the dependence of Ku(X, L) on the chosen exceptional collection and the relevant semiorthogonal decompositions, is set up in Proposition 3.7 and Example 3.8. The reason this is the right target is made explicit in Remark 4.6(ii): a positive answer to Question 3.9(iii) would let one drop the Fourier-Mukai-type assumption in the Enriques categorical Torelli theorem, Theorem 4.5.
